title: 反相比例放大器：虚短与虚断
statement: 图示为理想运放构成的反相比例放大器，u_s = 1 V，R1 = 10 kΩ，Rf = 40 kΩ。
求 R1 中的电流 i1（参考方向见图）和输出电压 u_o（o 端对地）。

questions.explain: 虚短：u_− = u_+ = 0（同相端接地，反相端为“虚地”），所以 i1 = (u_s − 0)/R1 = 1/10k = 0.1 mA。
虚断：流入反相端的电流为零，i_f = i1。u_o = u_− − Rf·i_f = 0 − 40k × 0.1 mA = −4 V，即 u_o = −(Rf/R1)·u_s。

questions.ask: 关于反相输入端结点 n，下列说法正确的是？
choices: n 点电位为零（虚地），但它并没有真的接地
n 点用导线接地，所以电位为零
questions.explain: n 点电位为零是因为“虚短”（u_− = u_+ = 0），并不是真的有导线接地；正因为“虚断”，R1 的电流不会流进运放，只能全部经过 Rf。

hints: 理想运放两条规则：虚短 u_− = u_+；虚断 i_− = i_+ = 0。
同相端接地，所以反相端 n 也是 0 V；R1 的电流全部流过 Rf。
solution: **1. 虚短。** 同相端接地，u_+ = 0，所以 u_n = u_− = 0（虚地）。
**3. 虚断。** 反相端不取电流，对结点 n 列 KCL：i_f = i1 = 0.1 mA。
一般地 u_o = −(Rf/R1)·u_s = −4 × 1 V，“−”号表示输出与输入反相。

en.title: Inverting amplifier: virtual short and virtual open
statement: The ideal op-amp forms an inverting amplifier with u_s = 1 V, R1 = 10 kΩ, Rf = 40 kΩ.
Find the current i1 in R1 (reference direction as drawn) and the output voltage u_o (terminal o to ground).

questions.explain: Virtual short: v− = v+ = 0 (the non-inverting input is grounded, so the inverting input is a "virtual ground"). Hence i1 = (u_s − 0)/R1 = 1/10k = 0.1 mA.
Virtual open: no current enters the inverting input, so i_f = i1. u_o = v− − Rf·i_f = 0 − 40k × 0.1 mA = −4 V, i.e. u_o = −(Rf/R1)·u_s.

questions.ask: Which statement about the inverting-input node n is true?
choices: n is at 0 V (a virtual ground), but it is not actually connected to ground
n is wired to ground, so it is at 0 V
n is at the potential u_s
questions.explain: n is at 0 V because of the virtual short (v− = v+ = 0), not because of a wire to ground. Because of the virtual open, the current in R1 cannot enter the op-amp and must all flow through Rf.

hints: The two rules of the ideal op-amp: virtual short v− = v+; virtual open i− = i+ = 0.
The non-inverting input is grounded, so node n is at 0 V too; all of R1's current goes on through Rf.
solution: **1. Virtual short.** v+ = 0, so u_n = v− = 0 (virtual ground).
**3. Virtual open.** The inverting input draws no current; KCL at n: i_f = i1 = 0.1 mA.
In general u_o = −(Rf/R1)·u_s = −4 × 1 V; the minus sign means the output is inverted.
